headline: ServiceNow has launched AI Passport, a credential system meant to let companies verify and control AI agents at each step of a workflow.
score_reason: Company product launch; read through one trade outlet, ServiceNow's own release was blocked, and the benefits are the company's claims.
importance_line: Companies worried about AI agents going out of bounds get a way to check agent credentials, with Nvidia as launch partner, but it is new and untested at scale.
summary: CIO Dive reports that ServiceNow unveiled AI Passport on Thursday, built on open specifications, so that governance products, identity providers and enforcement points can verify credentials for company and third-party agents at every step of a multi-agent workflow. ServiceNow is working with Nvidia as design and launch partner, using the Nvidia Open Agent Safety Platform, and also added AI governance features such as shadow AI detection and AI cost management.
notes: Investing.com original blocked (403), ServiceNow and Techzine pages also blocked; CIO Dive column read instead. Its coverage is a short section of a roundup.
